privacy.title: Your words never touch anyone's server
privacy.p1: Speech is recognized on your phone; DropVoice sends only text over a peer-to-peer WebRTC DataChannel — no cloud in between.
privacy.p2: The public pairing server relays handshake signals only while connecting, and never sees your content.
privacy.note: Traffic within your LAN is unencrypted — use trusted networks.
privacy.cloudCaption: Recognition and storage happen on someone else's server
privacy.p2pCaption: Text goes P2P, never leaves your LAN
privacy.handshakeCaption: The pairing server carries handshakes only

devices.title: One phone, every PC you own
devices.p1: Pair each machine once; afterwards a single tap on its color dot switches where your words go.

selfhost.title: Run the pairing server on your own machine
selfhost.p1: The whole rendezvous service is one container image. Prefer not to use the public server? It runs on yours in three commands.
selfhost.p2: Open source isn't a gesture — you can read every line.
selfhost.fullSteps: Full steps live in the repo's docker/ directory

faq.title: FAQ
faq.a1: Recognition happens in your phone's own keyboard. DropVoice only carries the text — accuracy equals your phone's.
faq.a2: No. Speech is converted to text on the phone and sent peer-to-peer; there is no server of ours it could reach — we don't have one.
faq.a3: MIT licensed and free. No subscription, ever.
faq.a4: Windows, macOS and Linux installers; the phone side is a web app — scan and go.
faq.a5: Text travels peer-to-peer over your LAN, typically appearing within tens of milliseconds — close to typing.

final.title: Now, say something.
final.sub: Install the desktop app, scan once. The rest is just talking.
